## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.



```{r tidy-who-data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)

# Years to keep
start_year <- 2000
end_year <- 2015

# Read the WHO downloads
cases <- read_csv("Estimated number of malaria cases 2000-2015.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
itn <- read_csv("Prevention Insecticide-Treated Bed Net (2000-2024).csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Check the column names before cleaning
names(cases)
names(itn)
```


```{r filter-who-data}
# Keep WHO European Region countries and years 2000–2015
# Replace these example column names with your actual names.

european_countries <- c(
  "Albania", "Andorra", "Armenia", "Austria", "Azerbaijan",
  "Belarus", "Belgium", "Bosnia and Herzegovina", "Bulgaria",
  "Croatia", "Cyprus", "Czechia", "Denmark", "Estonia",
  "Finland", "France", "Georgia", "Germany", "Greece",
  "Hungary", "Iceland", "Ireland", "Israel", "Italy",
  "Kazakhstan", "Kyrgyzstan", "Latvia", "Lithuania",
  "Luxembourg", "Malta", "Monaco", "Montenegro",
  "Netherlands", "North Macedonia", "Norway", "Poland",
  "Portugal", "Republic of Moldova", "Romania", "Russian Federation",
  "San Marino", "Serbia", "Slovakia", "Slovenia", "Spain",
  "Sweden", "Switzerland", "Tajikistan", "Türkiye", "Turkmenistan",
  "Ukraine", "United Kingdom", "Uzbekistan"
)

cases_clean <- cases |>
  rename(
    country = Location,
    year = Period,
    value = Value
  ) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) |>
  filter(
    year >= start_year,
    year <= end_year,
    country %in% european_countries
  )

# Save cleaned dataset
write_csv(cases_clean, "Estimated number of malaria cases 2000-2015.csv")

# View result
head(cases_clean)
```
